title: At 21, should I buy a 430 sq ft suite in KL with RM80,000 cashback?
excerpt: A 21-year-old wants a tiny dual-key suite on Jalan Ampang for Airbnb, financed with a big cashback. Sean lists the numbers he must check first, and says missing a deal beats a 35-year mistake.

question.asker: From A, a viewer who wrote in by email
question.context: A is 21 and new to the channel. He is considering a 430 sq ft dual-key suite on Jalan Ampang with a RM410,000 loan and RM80,000 cashback. He would use the cashback to furnish the unit and keep a reserve. He plans to run it on Airbnb, since he doubts anyone would live long-term in so small a space, and worries he can't otherwise afford a property.
question.text: Is this a good first investment, or is he making a mistake that will become a financial burden?

answer.quote: Would you rather have missed a deal or would you live with a mistake?
answer.summary: He hasn't done the homework yet, and at 21 he doesn't need to own property. He should first work out the real rents, nightly rates, occupancy and price per square foot against nearby projects, and check he could survive six months with no guest. Only buy if the numbers clearly cover the instalment.

reasons.title: Cheap is not the same as a good deal
reasons.body: A good deal is priced below market value and either earns cash flow, has strong potential to appreciate, or is structured for the cashback. After the cashback this unit costs about RM330,000, which may be RM900 to RM1,000 psf when neighbours sell at about RM700.

reasons.title: Airbnb needs its own maths
reasons.body: A RM410,000 loan costs about RM2,000 a month. He needs the nightly rate, an occupancy of perhaps 70% to 80%, and the operator's cut, and must check that the building still allows short stays, as some ban them.

reasons.title: Every property needs a plan B and C
reasons.body: If short stays fail, who would rent it long-term, and can a 430 sq ft unit be split further? Thousands of similar small units nearby, and auctions in the area, could push rents down.

reasons.title: At 21, flexibility is worth more
reasons.body: Start with an emergency fund of six months, insurance and a stable career. Starting at 25 or 28 with real data is no loss.

actions: Collect long-term rents and nightly rates for similar units on Jalan Ampang.
Ask operators about real occupancy and their profit split, and check the building's rules on short stays.
Compare the price per square foot with neighbouring projects.
Make sure you can pay the instalment for six months with no income from the unit.
View about 20 projects before booking any of them.
caveat: Sean has nothing against small units or high risk. If the data shows the rent comfortably covers the instalment and he can afford six empty months, going ahead is a calculated risk.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #197. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in January 2023.
